command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent read the PDF, identified the corresponding author (Tianlin Shi), but spent 20+ turns struggling to switch from the Evince PDF viewer to Chrome. Eventually reached scholar.google.com loading page but ran out of turns (50 turns, 337s).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can read PDF content, navigate PDF pages, identify author names, type URLs in Chrome address bar, scroll within documents
metadata.failure_analysis: Model could not efficiently switch from Evince PDF viewer to Chrome browser. Repeatedly clicked on taskbar icons, Activities button, and tried keyboard shortcuts (Alt+Tab, Super) without success. The core failure was app-switching, not comprehension or navigation.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplest decomposition of original task: just navigate to Google Scholar in Chrome. Tests the core capability the model failed at (switching to Chrome and navigating to a URL) without the additional complexity of reading the PDF.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to scholar.google.com in Chrome. Evaluator checks if the active Chrome tab URL contains 'scholar.google.com' using the standard is_expected_url_pattern_match metric with active_url_from_accessTree getter.

scoring_breakdown.navigation: 1.0 - Chrome active tab URL contains scholar.google.com

llm_judge_reasons: Getter active_url_from_accessTree correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL from the accessibility tree, which is exactly the state needed to verify navigation to scholar.google.com.

Metric is_expected_url_pattern_match correctly receives the rules dict with 'expected' key containing regex patterns, and performs regex search against the URL. The pattern 'scholar\.google\.com' will correctly match any URL on Google Scholar.
The instruction has a single requirement (open scholar.google.com in Chrome) and the evaluator fully covers it with URL pattern matching.
No postconfig needed since the URL state persists after the agent finishes. No state timing issues.
Expected parameter handling is correct: get_rule returns config['rules'] = {'expected': ['scholar\.google\.com']}, and the metric accesses rules['expected'] directly.
